GDX.summary: GDX closed Friday at $80.20, below its 20-, 50- and 200-day moving averages (86.57 / 92.86 / 90.94), with RSI at 34.5, close to oversold. It sits in the lower part of its $67.79–$115.84 52-week range. Gold fell about 4% this week, its worst week since June, and spot gold slipped under $4,000 for the first time since mid-July. Most of the selling came on Thursday, driven by an oil rally on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, higher-for-longer Fed rate bets and margin-call selling tied to the tech selloff. Newmont, GDX's top holding, beat Q3 estimates with adjusted EPS of $2.20 and $1.9B of free cash flow, but miners still fell with bullion. Next week brings the Oct 27–28 FOMC (decision Oct 28, 2:00 PM ET; markets price a hold but a likely December hike) and PCE inflation data on Oct 29.
bullets: Bull case: RSI is near oversold, analysts see the selloff as liquidity- and stop-driven rather than fundamental, speculative positioning may be near an extreme, and Newmont's record Q3 shows strong miner margins at about $4,000 gold.

Bear case: a hawkish FOMC or hot PCE could lift yields and the dollar again. Saxo watches $3,970 as gold's next support, and GDX is below all three key moving averages, so the trend still points down.
